# Background
TechVenture Inc., a rapidly growing SaaS company, is seeking external funding. The CFO has asked you to complete a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation to determine the enterprise value of the company.

The company has provided historical financial data for 2023 and detailed assumptions for projecting future performance. Your task is to build the valuation model by calculating present values of future free cash flows and the terminal value.

# Task
Complete the DCF valuation model to calculate the enterprise value of TechVenture Inc.

Specifically, you need to:
1. Calculate the present value (PV) of projected free cash flows for years 2024-2028
2. Calculate the terminal value using the Gordon Growth Model
3. Calculate the present value of the terminal value
4. Sum all components to arrive at the enterprise value

# Requirements
- Use the WACC (Weighted Average Cost of Capital) provided in the Assumptions sheet as the discount rate
- Apply the appropriate discount factors for each year (Year 1 through Year 5)
- The terminal value should be calculated using the perpetual growth rate specified in the Assumptions sheet
- Discount the terminal value back to present value using the Year 5 discount factor
- Place the final enterprise value calculation in cell B19 of the DCF_Model sheet

# Tips
- The free cash flow projections (row 10) are already calculated for you
- Discount factor formula: 1 / (1 + WACC)^year
- Gordon Growth Model: Terminal Value = FCF_year5 × (1 + g) / (WACC - g)
- All intermediate calculations should use cell references, not hardcoded values

# Deliverable
Complete the DCF_Model sheet with all valuation calculations showing your work in the designated cells.
criteria: Enterprise value calculated correctly in DCF_Model!B19
Present value of projected FCF (sum of years 2024-2028) calculated correctly in DCF_Model!B16
Terminal value calculated using Gordon Growth Model in DCF_Model!B17
Present value of terminal value discounted correctly in DCF_Model!B18
All discount factors applied correctly using WACC from Assumptions sheet
All calculations use proper cell references, not hardcoded values
